content: The recommended dosage for ORAVIG is one 50 mg buccal tablet applied to the upper gum area, specifically the canine fossa, once daily for a total of 14 consecutive days. ORAVIG should be applied in the morning after the patient has brushed their teeth. The tablet must be handled with dry hands. The rounded side of the tablet should be placed against the upper gum, just above the incisor tooth in the canine fossa region. Although the tablet is rounded on one side for comfort, either side of the tablet can be used for application. Once applied, the ORAVIG tablet will remain in position and gradually dissolve over time. For subsequent applications, the tablet should be placed on the opposite side of the mouth to alternate the application site. Before applying the next dose, any residual material from the previous tablet should be removed. The ORAVIG tablet should not be crushed, chewed, or swallowed. Patients can eat and drink normally while the tablet is in place; however, chewing gum should be avoided. If the ORAVIG tablet does not adhere properly or falls off within the first 6 hours of application, the same tablet should be repositioned immediately. If the tablet still fails to adhere, a new tablet should be applied. If the tablet is accidentally swallowed within the first 6 hours, the patient should drink a glass of water and apply a new tablet, but this should only be done once. If the tablet falls off or is swallowed after it has been in place for 6 hours or more, a new tablet should not be applied until the next scheduled dose.
